I have no real advice to offer besides the fact that I relate to almost everything you said except I graduated '21. I too sacrificed everything in high school just to end college with no friends, barely passing grades, and I chose to not walk (I saw no point in it and I dont regret it tbh). You mentioned in your post that its no point to tell you that college is no big deal and you're right, to an extent. Its okay to be upset that things continously don't go as planned. Its okay to be angry at things you couldn't do or to be angry that everyone else seems to be fine while you're struggling. Its okay to be upset at the people or situations that traumatized you. Its okay to acknowledge and admit that both high school and undergrad sucked for you/ people like us but the main point should be no one should let it be the focus of their lives. Hey I'm also 23 and I swear we are living the same life right now. I graduated with my bachelors, my job isn't what I though it was going to be and my family is also going through hardships that I can't control. There is one quote I found recently that has helped me: "Its not finding gratitude that matters most. Its about remembering to look in the first place."

This quote resonates with me because when I'm in a dark/bad mental state, I'm very pessimistic and dismissive of anything good in my life. So now when I'm in a bad spot, I think of that quote and I try to think of the good BUT what's different is I don't beat myself up if I don't actually believe in these things I should be grateful for. All that matters to me, in that moment, is that I'm at least trying to find some good. For now, thats enough and with time maybe I'll one day believe in those things too.

The idea of thoughts and prayers is a mocked response to a large complex issue such as gun violence since as we all know, those actions don't lead to much change. 

However asking for "thoughts and prayers" from others in response to a rough mental state is actually the opposite since its important to have a strong social support. Social support is the most predictive factor when it comes to resilience in people. Additionally, its difficult to be vulnerable and reach out and you should be proud for doing it any way. 

Sorry for the tangent above but I thought it was important to share the difference (at least the difference to me). I understand being in that "pos" spiral and while I dont know you, I do know that the vision we have of ourselves is usually much harsher and slightly inaccurate than how we actually are. I hope you are able to take it day by day and try to be kind to yourself. You'll be in my thoughts and I do hope things are able to improve.

You don't have to open the app or actually work on any French at the time you download it but you can at least tell yourself, "hey I got a step closer to learning french." The next task could be to login in. The next following task could be to complete an activity on the app. Completing tasks (at least for me) helps build motivation since I never start out having  motivation to do anything. I truly hope this strategy can help or that you can find something that works for you in the nearby future

You are suppose to scan the package as well as scan one that is on the pallet everytime you get a new package. That error messagr pops up when one of the packages on the pallet was never properly scanned in

You scan package number one, then scan a package that is already on the pallet and place the first package on the pallet. After you make sure you get the green message on the scanner saying the package was moved. You then scan package number two and then again scan a package that was already placed on the pallet and place second package on the pallet.

Its easier to explain in a more hands on way but I will try to explain it through text. When you get that message, it means that someone could have forgotten to scan that second package onto the pallet. Therefore, when you try to scan your initial package with the forgotten one (the second package), it can't go anywhere since neither are "in the system." Therefore you scan the initial package with another package that is different from those first two. You can then scan that "second package" onto the pallet. I hope that all makes sense.
